insights.headline: The d-squared law's predicted FLEX burn time has a median of 0.951 times the measured one, across 196 tests. That is a median ratio, not an error bound.
insights.detail: For the 196 FLEX tests that list a starting diameter, an extinction diameter, a burning rate and a burn time, the predicted burn time divided by the measured one has a median of 0.951. Half of the tests fall between 0.916 and 0.975. The median shows where the middle of the tests sits and says nothing about the error of any one test. Each prediction uses the burning rate and the diameters from its own row, so this checks that the table agrees with the law. It is not an independent test of a fire model. The burning rate column lost its unit in the file. EMBER reads it as mm² per second.
insights.formula: Predicted burn time = (d0² − dExt²) ÷ K. The ratio is predicted ÷ measured.

insights.headline: In FLEX, flames went out in 27 of 28 droplet tests at 10 to 15% oxygen and in 2 of 24 at 28 to 36%.

These counts mix fuels, pressures and added gases, so they show a direction and not a limit.
insights.formula: A count of the Test end column by oxygen band. A band such as 10 to 15% runs from 10 up to, and not including, 15.

insights.headline: 186 of 274 FLEX droplet tests ended with the visible flame going out before the fuel was gone.
insights.detail: Methanol, 157 tests: 126 extinction, 23 disruption, 8 completion. Heptane, 117 tests: 60 extinction, 38 disruption, 19 completion. Extinction means the visible flame went out. Disruption means the droplet broke up. Completion means it burned away. A flame going out is not proof that all burning stopped, because FLEX also found cool flames.
insights.formula: A count of the Test end column, by fuel.
